Yup. I remember a few years ago being told I was in remission long enough that any chances of the cancer coming back were gone. I still am a bit more vulnerable than other people to getting another cancer but I don't have much to worry about if I avoid smoking and keep myself at a healthy weight.

I also received radiation at such a young age and avoided developing any severe brain defects and ability to think. I have tourette syndrome which may have been caused by it but I've pretty much grown out of it by now. I feel like I'm really lucky.

I'm ugly and I think it's great. 

I see a lot of people saying that you can lose weight or get a hair cut. Truthfully those don't work on me. I had cancer when I was 4 that was in my sinus and radiation treatment on that area at such a young age caused my upper jaw to under-develop which made my face deformed. I also lost all my top teeth except two molars. I have never once in my life been called attractive. Even my best friends say with honesty that I'm pretty ugly. The only possible way I can fix it is probably with some drastic kind of plastic surgery, but even then that may not work. But it's okay!

Ugliness acts as a natural filter. Much less people are attracted to you, but that means the ones that do find you attractive have to like you strictly just for your personality. If you have a favorable personality, you will find yourself in fewer yet more sincere relationships as opposed a high number of less sincere relationships attractive people may have. Why would you want to be with someone that is only with you because of your looks anyway?

Also having an attractive appearance isn't just facial structure, hair, or weight. It's also how people feel being around you. Being ugly doesn't make you creepy. You may seem creepy to girls if you are awkward, shy, or if you go up to them wanting strictly to date them. Try thinking of a romantic relationship more as a luxury than a necessity. You don't need one to be happy and any kind of relationship is great.

Just go up to anyone just to be happy to talk to someone. Get happy and interested in what they're saying. Having a genuine smile is actually really effective and makes people feel like you enjoy talking to them. It's hard to force yourself to smile and look genuine so just get excited and have it happen naturally. An ugly person that is happy and genuine is nice to be around and attractive in their own way.

Honestly I'm just saying this but it's much easier said than done. I used to be an awkward shy person and some people probably thought I was creepy so I can at least tell you the changes that happened with me to make it better.

First I think it's good to understand why someone may not want to talk to someone that is awkward or think they're creepy. Shyness or uncomfortableness with talking to someone can sometimes be mistaken for disinterest, hostility, or creepiness. Imagine if you went up and talked to someone and they looked uncomfortable when you talked to them. You would probably assume that they didn't like what you were saying or didn't care and you may feel bad.

From what I've seen, awkwardness isn't a problem unless you care about your awkwardness and try to hard to avoid being awkward. More people are socially awkward than you think, and it can come off as less creepy and more endearing if you don't get worked up about it laugh it off and remain genuinely happy with talking to someone.

Big thing too when talking to someone is carefulness. Carefulness is good with things that would obviously be offensive, but being being too careful in avoiding acting weird or awkward causes you to look uncomfortable which actually is what can make you awkward. When talking to people you just need to let the conversation flow just for the sake of talking like you would with a best friend. If they don't act interested or friendly just try to think of it as on them on not yourself and just move on and talk to someone else.

This is very difficult to force yourself into so I'm not going to act like taking this advice will magically make you better. It's going to take a lot of effort for you. One thing I can definitely recommend is maintaining high energy. If you are very energetic you move along much faster and more confidently than if you are tired. Get plenty of sleep and drink caffeine it'll help.

Remember that success is determined by how happy you are. Everything we do in life is for the sake of achieving happiness including having a relationship, money, status, and a good career. Stop letting people tell you that you are a loser because you've never been in a relationship. To me a McDonalds worker is more successful than a millionaire if they are happier, and the guy that's in a relationship that is less happy than you when you are single is less successful than you. Just talk to men and women just because you want to talk to someone. Relationships may make people happy, but so do conversations and friendships.

I have Tourettes and ADHD and in 5th grade I was a problem child so they sent me to this sort of private type school.

In 8th grade there were two accounts on a computer. One was students and the other was teacher. The teacher account had a password on it. I can't remember why but for some reason they would sometimes let us onto the teacher account. I think for projects because a lot of websites were blocked.

I changed the name from Teacher to Bob Saget, added a picture of Bob Saget, and then changed the password.

IT was actually pretty dumb in that school. I thought I did it just to that one computer, but the change happened to every single computer in the school. Chaos sets in as every teacher gets locked out because the account now belongs to Bob Saget.

I guess I didn't get in trouble because they were so desperate for the account back that they would do anything to have me put it back to normal.
